findings.title: Access-controlled Environment variable file path exists
findings.description: The path '/.env' returned HTTP 403, indicating the environment variable file exists but is protected by access controls. While direct access is restricted, its existence confirms the presence of a sensitive resource and remains a target for authentication bypass.
findings.remediation: Consider removing '/.env' entirely rather than relying on access controls alone. A file that should not exist should not exist — not be hidden.

findings.title: Access-controlled Git repository config path exists
findings.description: The path '/.git/config' returned HTTP 403, indicating the git repository config exists but is protected by access controls. While direct access is restricted, its existence confirms the presence of a sensitive resource and remains a target for authentication bypass.
findings.remediation: Consider removing '/.git/config' entirely rather than relying on access controls alone. A file that should not exist should not exist — not be hidden.

findings.title: Access-controlled Git repository listing path exists
findings.description: The path '/.git/' returned HTTP 403, indicating the git repository listing exists but is protected by access controls. While direct access is restricted, its existence confirms the presence of a sensitive resource and remains a target for authentication bypass.
findings.remediation: Consider removing '/.git/' entirely rather than relying on access controls alone. A file that should not exist should not exist — not be hidden.

findings.title: Sensitive path disclosed in robots.txt Disallow
findings.description: The robots.txt Disallow directive reveals the path '/config', which appears to be a sensitive or restricted area. robots.txt is a public document readable by anyone, so Disallow directives inadvertently advertise the existence of these paths to attackers and search engine crawlers alike.
findings.remediation: Do not rely on robots.txt to protect sensitive paths — it provides no access control and actively reveals the paths it tries to hide. Protect sensitive areas with authentication and authorization instead. Consider removing sensitive paths from Disallow directives.

findings.title: Content-Security-Policy header missing
findings.description: No Content-Security-Policy (CSP) header was found. CSP is a critical defence-in-depth mechanism that limits the impact of cross-site scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks.
findings.remediation: Add a strict Content-Security-Policy header. Start with: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'

findings.title: HSTS max-age is below 1 year
findings.description: The Strict-Transport-Security max-age is 0 seconds (0 days), which is below the recommended minimum of 1 year (31,536,000 seconds).
findings.remediation: Set max-age to at least 31536000 (1 year).

findings.title: HSTS does not include subdomains
findings.description: The Strict-Transport-Security header is missing 'includeSubDomains'. Subdomains remain vulnerable to downgrade attacks even when the main domain is protected.
findings.remediation: Add 'includeSubDomains' to the HSTS header.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options header missing
findings.description: Neither X-Frame-Options nor a CSP frame-ancestors directive was found. The page may be embedded in an iframe on an attacker-controlled site (clickjacking).
findings.remediation:
Add: X-Frame-Options: DENY
Or use CSP: Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'

findings.title: Referrer-Policy header missing
findings.description: No Referrer-Policy header was found. Browsers default to 'no-referrer-when-downgrade', potentially leaking full URL paths to third-party sites via the Referer header.
findings.remediation: Add: Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin

findings.title: Permissions-Policy header missing
findings.description: No Permissions-Policy header was found. Without it, all browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation, etc.) default to their browser-specified policy, which may be permissive.
findings.remediation: Add a Permissions-Policy header restricting unused features. Example: Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()

findings.title: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy (COOP) header missing
findings.description: COOP prevents cross-origin windows from retaining a reference to this page, protecting against cross-origin attacks such as XS-Leaks.
findings.remediation: Add: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin

findings.title: Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy (COEP) header missing
findings.description: COEP prevents a document from loading cross-origin resources that don't explicitly grant permission. Required to enable powerful features like SharedArrayBuffer.
findings.remediation: Add: Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp

findings.title: Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy (CORP) header missing
findings.description: CORP restricts which origins may embed this resource. Without it, any site can embed this page's resources, enabling Spectre-style side-channel reads.
findings.remediation: Add: Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin

findings.title: Technology disclosed via server header
findings.description: The response header 'server: Squarespace' discloses the server/platform technology. This aids attacker reconnaissance.

findings.title: Content-Security-Policy header missing
findings.description: No Content-Security-Policy (CSP) header was found. CSP is a critical defence-in-depth mechanism that limits the impact of cross-site scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks.
findings.remediation: Add a strict Content-Security-Policy header. Start with: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'

findings.title: HSTS max-age is below 1 year
findings.description: The Strict-Transport-Security max-age is 0 seconds (0 days), which is below the recommended minimum of 1 year (31,536,000 seconds).
findings.remediation: Set max-age to at least 31536000 (1 year).

findings.title: HSTS does not include subdomains
findings.description: The Strict-Transport-Security header is missing 'includeSubDomains'. Subdomains remain vulnerable to downgrade attacks even when the main domain is protected.
findings.remediation: Add 'includeSubDomains' to the HSTS header.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options header missing
findings.description: Neither X-Frame-Options nor a CSP frame-ancestors directive was found. The page may be embedded in an iframe on an attacker-controlled site (clickjacking).
findings.remediation:
Add: X-Frame-Options: DENY
Or use CSP: Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'

findings.title: Referrer-Policy header missing
findings.description: No Referrer-Policy header was found. Browsers default to 'no-referrer-when-downgrade', potentially leaking full URL paths to third-party sites via the Referer header.
findings.remediation: Add: Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin

findings.title: Permissions-Policy header missing
findings.description: No Permissions-Policy header was found. Without it, all browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation, etc.) default to their browser-specified policy, which may be permissive.
findings.remediation: Add a Permissions-Policy header restricting unused features. Example: Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()

findings.title: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy (COOP) header missing
findings.description: COOP prevents cross-origin windows from retaining a reference to this page, protecting against cross-origin attacks such as XS-Leaks.
findings.remediation: Add: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin

findings.title: Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy (COEP) header missing
findings.description: COEP prevents a document from loading cross-origin resources that don't explicitly grant permission. Required to enable powerful features like SharedArrayBuffer.
findings.remediation: Add: Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp

findings.title: Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy (CORP) header missing
findings.description: CORP restricts which origins may embed this resource. Without it, any site can embed this page's resources, enabling Spectre-style side-channel reads.
findings.remediation: Add: Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin

findings.title: Technology disclosed via server header
findings.description: The response header 'server: Squarespace' discloses the server/platform technology. This aids attacker reconnaissance.

findings.title: Large base64 blob in inline script
findings.description: An inline script contains a base64-encoded blob of 104 characters. Large base64 strings in inline scripts often carry obfuscated payloads (shellcode, packed JavaScript, exfiltration data).
findings.remediation: Investigate the source of the base64 string. Decode and review its content. Remove if unexpected or injected.

findings.title: SPF record missing for chicagopepperbros.com
findings.description: No SPF (Sender Policy Framework) TXT record was found for 'chicagopepperbros.com'. Without SPF, attackers can forge email from this domain, enabling phishing and spam campaigns.
findings.remediation: Add an SPF TXT record. Example: v=spf1 include:_spf.yourdomain.com -all

findings.title: DMARC record missing for chicagopepperbros.com
findings.description: No DMARC record was found at '_dmarc.chicagopepperbros.com'. Without DMARC, there is no policy to reject or quarantine spoofed email and no visibility into abuse of the domain.
findings.remediation: Add a DMARC TXT record at _dmarc.{domain}. Start with monitoring: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@yourdomain.com. Progressively tighten to p=quarantine then p=reject.
